settings.heading: We never really planned this.
settings.body:
We never really planned this.

Elysian Groove started in 2024 with three friends, a beach restaurant and an idea that was supposed to be much smaller than what it became.

Rodrigo and Francisco were part of the student association at FCT NOVA and wanted to organize a simple afternoon with music. Martim was working at his father’s beach restaurant, Café do Mar, on the south side of Lisbon.

The conversation was pretty straightforward:

Why make a small gathering when we could just throw a party?

So we did.

We invited some friends, put tickets online for €3 and hoped people would show up. Around 300 did.

It wasn’t a huge production. There wasn’t a sophisticated concept behind it. It was just music, friends, the beach and a feeling that something different was happening.

And people loved it.

At the time, there wasn’t much like it happening on our side of the river. So we did it again. And again.

What started as a few summer parties at Café do Mar slowly became something people associated with summer itself. You knew the place, you knew the people and you knew what was going to happen when Elysian Groove was there.

It became a kind of summer ritual.

Crossing the bridge

But then summer ended. And we weren’t ready for Elysian Groove to end with it.

Winter forced us to answer the first real question about Elysian Groove: was this just a summer thing?

We decided to find out.

Our first move outside Café do Mar took us across the river to 8 Marvila, where we partnered with Poetry List. More than a thousand people showed up.

For us, that night changed everything. It proved that people weren’t only coming because of the beach, the weather or Café do Mar. They were coming for something we had started building without fully realizing it.

Elysian Groove could exist anywhere.

Around the same time, we started noticing parties escaping clubs — appearing inside cafés, restaurants, pizza places and everyday spaces never designed to become dance floors. We loved that idea and started doing our own version of it in Portugal.

Instead of waiting for people to discover Elysian Groove at an event, we wanted Elysian Groove to appear where nobody expected it.

Then came 2025

We started the year with Beca Beca, an open event that brought together more than 3,000 people. Then came Coliseu dos Recreios, alongside Temple of Dreams. And then Casa Nolita. Four thousand people. One stage. A few lights. And a wooden Elysian Groove sign that, somehow, none of us noticed was spelled wrong.

We’ve never tried to pretend everything was perfect. We were learning while doing it. Every event became slightly bigger, slightly crazier and slightly more ambitious than the one before it.

One year later

For our first anniversary, we went to Escala 25, underneath Ponte 25 de Abril, for our first real large-scale production. Almost 2,000 people came.

From there, Elysian Groove kept moving: Belice, Loft Marvila and two events at LX Factory. Different spaces, different formats, different crowds, but always the same idea: the location should be part of the experience.

Lisbon became our playground

What began with 300 people at a beach restaurant eventually became thousands of people gathering in some of Lisbon’s most recognizable places. In 2026, we took over MAAT Central for a ticketed event with around 4,000 people. Then came our second anniversary in Belém, at Praça Amália Rodrigues e o Fado.

Today, Elysian Groove is bigger than the three of us and bigger than any individual event. It’s the thousands of people who show up, the artists, the venues, the videos, the ridiculous ideas that somehow make it into production and the moments nobody planned.

We started on a beach with €3 tickets. We have no idea exactly where this ends. That’s kind of the point.
settings.closing_text: What if we threw a party here?
